works.citation: Wei, Rong, and Tim Summers. 2026. The Chinese Government’s Negotiating Strategy Over the Future of Hong Kong: Revisiting the 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration. The International History Review 48(1):134–151. First online 17 February 2025.
works.version_read: Complete publisher version of record, 2026 issue pagination; CC BY 4.0
works.retrieval_note: Public publisher HTML and PDF accessible through browser. Save completed before a later native-app inspection hung; downloaded PDF subsequently recovered and hashed. No login, CAPTCHA, paywall bypass or new archive acquisition.

physical_extent.mapping: PDF 1 is publisher cover; printed = PDF + 132 for PDF 2–19

sequential_coverage.scope: Full publisher HTML read in sequence: abstract, introduction, I–IV, conclusion, all 138 notes, disclosure and contributor statements. Complete PDF native text then read and checked against HTML.

works.unresolved_ocr: None material; native PDF text and HTML available. Visual inspection was selective, not full-facsimile coverage.
works.methodology_read: Historical interpretive reconstruction, explicitly thin constructivist. Chinese participant memoirs and oral histories supplemented by UK, Hong Kong and US materials. No cross-case causal estimate; relevant Chinese MFA archives unavailable. Article explicitly labels findings provisional and warns of memoir scrutiny/amendment (136,139–140).
works.empirical_window: Primarily 1979–1984 Sino-British negotiations, with earlier historical context. Later conclusion comments do not constitute a post-1984 behavioral dataset.

claims.finding: Chinese research and business-elite liaison supply an alternative to the British inference that rejection of continuing UK administration showed ignorance of capitalism.
claims.assessment: Revise the original-period baseline: understanding an argument and accepting its proposed solution are separate.
claims.caveat: Retrospective memoir evidence; knowledge does not establish accuracy or later compliance.

claims.finding: British officials sought private American intermediaries; a 1 December 1982 US reply endorsed selective briefings and suggested possible Japanese business messengers.
claims.assessment: Code the same intermediary tactic on both sides before assigning Chinese uniqueness.
claims.caveat: Original cables not read; article records requests and approval, not proven delivery or effectiveness.

claims.finding: The reconstruction pairs a sovereignty commitment with flexibility on subordinate arrangements.
claims.assessment: Test the scope of principles issue by issue.
claims.caveat: Do not turn a retrospective description into proof of an immutable cultural mechanism.

claims.finding: Cradock describes Zhou Nan’s authoritative phone answers and faster agenda work in early summer 1983.
claims.assessment: A differentiated early baseline is needed before measuring subsequent professionalization.
claims.caveat: Note 104 says Zhou quotes Cradock; those two citations are not independent observations.

claims.finding: Firmness coexists with the article’s account of clear leadership objectives and a strong chain of command.
claims.assessment: Treat this as a candidate counterexample to inferring leadership conflict from rigidity.
claims.caveat: Local leverage and lease expiry compete with leadership organization as explanations.

claims.finding: The discussion distinguishes military leverage and Chinese perceptions of the 1983 currency crisis.
claims.assessment: Separate observable vulnerabilities from participants’ claims about deliberate manipulation.
claims.caveat: Thatcher’s urgency corroborates vulnerability; it does not prove Britain manufactured the crisis.
